summary: Luke Badiali reviewed Ashcombe's partner and intermediary relationships with James Whitlow and Sophie Archer. Even with a proprietary engine, advisers will still bring most deals, so the aim is to get earlier, off-market looks. We agreed a tiered intermediary programme and a referral network with accountants and lawyers.

discussion.keyPoints: Ashcombe sees deals from around 60 corporate finance boutiques, but 8 account for most of the volume.
James noted that regional accountants and solicitors know about succession issues years before a sale.
Sophie raised the risk of upsetting advisers if Ashcombe is seen to bypass them.

recommendations.recommendation: Tier intermediaries: top 8 get a named partner and quarterly meeting; the rest get the Founder Report and an annual catch-up.
Build a referral panel of 15 regional accountancy and law firms in the Midlands and North.
Give tier one intermediaries a one-page Ashcombe deal criteria sheet updated every 6 months.
Explore co-investment alliances with two family offices for larger platforms above £8m EBITDA.
Sponsor one sector trade association conference in facilities maintenance.

actions.action: Assign a named partner to each of the top 8 intermediaries

nextFocus: Look at portfolio company management, retention and add-on growth.
nextPreparation: James to bring the portfolio value creation plans for the current platforms.

tests.question: How many intermediaries are in tier one?
Where is the referral panel based?
Is the family office co-investment idea agreed?
